ingredients.name: Whole grain oat flakes
ingredients.summary: Whole grain oat flakes are minimally processed oats that provide fiber, complex carbohydrates, and some protein, and are generally considered safe and health-promoting for most people.
ingredients.details: Whole grain oats contain beta-glucan, a soluble fiber that can help support healthy cholesterol levels and promote satiety. They have a low to moderate glycemic impact compared with refined grains and provide vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants. People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should ensure the oats are certified gluten-free, as cross-contamination with gluten-containing grains can occur.

ingredients.name: Flax seeds
ingredients.summary: Flax seeds are nutrient-dense seeds rich in omega-3 fatty acids, fiber, and lignans, and are generally considered safe and beneficial when consumed in typical food amounts.
ingredients.details: Flax seeds can support heart health due to their alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) content and may help improve bowel regularity because of their high fiber content. They also contain phytoestrogens (lignans), which may have mild hormone-modulating effects, usually considered safe in normal dietary intake. People with certain hormone-sensitive conditions or those on blood-thinning medications should consult a healthcare professional before consuming large supplemental amounts.

ingredients.name: Chia seeds
ingredients.summary: Chia seeds are small seeds high in fiber, plant-based omega-3 fats, and minerals, and are generally safe and supportive of metabolic and digestive health.
ingredients.details: Chia seeds absorb water and form a gel, which can promote satiety and help regulate blood sugar response to meals. Their high fiber content supports digestive health, but sudden high intake may cause bloating or discomfort in sensitive individuals if not accompanied by adequate fluids. Allergic reactions are rare but possible, so new users should start with small amounts.

ingredients.name: Quinoa
ingredients.summary: Quinoa is a gluten-free pseudocereal rich in protein, fiber, and minerals, and is generally considered a safe and nutritious whole-grain alternative.
ingredients.details: Quinoa provides a relatively complete amino acid profile compared with many other plant foods and has a moderate glycemic impact, making it suitable for balanced blood sugar control when eaten in appropriate portions. Naturally occurring saponins on the outer coating can cause bitterness or mild digestive irritation in some people, but rinsing before cooking or processing typically removes most of them. It is generally well tolerated, including by people avoiding gluten.

ingredients.name: Amaranth flakes
ingredients.summary: Amaranth flakes are processed from the amaranth pseudocereal, offering protein, fiber, and minerals, and are generally safe and nutritious for most people.
ingredients.details: Amaranth is naturally gluten-free and provides higher protein and micronutrient content than many refined grains, supporting more stable energy and better nutrient density. Like other whole grains and pseudocereals, it contains some antinutrients (such as phytates), but these are usually not a concern in the context of a varied diet. It is typically well tolerated, though any grain-like food can rarely trigger individual sensitivities.
